question: Should core Skill Workshop add the public review action and fail-closed reviewed-version lifecycle semantics proposed by this PR?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but it introduces new core model/CLI API and deliberately changes what happens when a proposal is revised while an approval is pending; repository evidence cannot establish product acceptance without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the core review API
options.body: Accept the service-owned review action and fail-closed version binding, contingent on rebase and live current-head proof.

options.title: Keep summary-only approvals
options.body: Decline or narrow the feature so core retains the current inspect and metadata-only approval contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core review API
recommendation.body: Accept the service-owned review action and fail-closed version binding, contingent on rebase and live current-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the most recent lifecycle-approval design and current Workshop CLI work, making them the best available decision owner for the new core contract.
